text: Now about spiritual gifts, brothers and sisters: I do not want you to be uninformed.
You know that when you were pagans, you were somehow enticed and led astray to idols that cannot speak.

versions.text: You know that when you were pagans, you were dragged along to mute idols, however you were led.
versions.explanation: The current wording puts the two verbs of leading in an odd order ("dragged along... however you were led"), which stumbles when read aloud. The Greek combines ἤγεσθε ἀπαγόμενοι into a single idea of being carried away/led astray, with ὡς ἄν expressing an indefinite "somehow." Also "idols that cannot speak" renders τὰ ἄφωνα more clearly for oral hearing than "mute idols."

text: So I want you to understand this: no one speaking by the Spirit of God says, "Jesus be cursed," and no one can say, "Jesus is Lord," except by the Holy Spirit.
There are different gifts, but the same Spirit;
and there are different ministries, but the same Lord;
and there are different activities, but the same God, who works all of them in everyone.
To each person the manifestation of the Spirit is given for the common good.
To one is given through the Spirit a word of wisdom, to another a word of knowledge by the same Spirit,
to another faith by the same Spirit, to another gifts of healing by the one Spirit,
to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another the discerning of spirits, to another different kinds of tongues, to another the interpretation of tongues.
All these are the work of one and the same Spirit, who distributes them to each one individually as he wills.
For just as the body is one and yet has many parts, and all the parts of the body, though many, form one body, so it is with Christ.
For we were all baptized by one Spirit into one body—whether Jews or Greeks, slaves or free—and we were all given the one Spirit to drink.
Indeed, the body is not made up of one part but of many.
If the foot should say, "Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body," would that make it any less a part of the body?
And if the ear should say, "Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body," that would not make it any less a part of the body.
If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be? If the whole body were an ear, where would the sense of smell be?
But in fact God has placed the parts, each one of them, in the body just as he wanted.
If they were all one part, where would the body be?
As it is, there are many parts, but one body.
The eye cannot say to the hand, "I have no need of you," nor can the head say to the feet, "I have no need of you."
On the contrary, the parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable,
and the parts we consider less honorable we clothe with greater honor; the parts we would rather not display we treat with special modesty,
while our presentable parts need no such care. But God has put the body together, giving greater honor to the part that lacked it,
so that there should be no division in the body, but that its parts should have the same concern for one another.
If one part suffers, every part suffers with it; if one part is honored, every part rejoices with it.
Now you are the body of Christ, and each one of you is a part of it.
And in the church God has appointed first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracles, then gifts of healing, forms of help, forms of leadership, and different kinds of tongues.

versions.text: And in the church God has appointed first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracles, then gifts of healing, of helping, of guiding, and different kinds of tongues.
versions.explanation: ἀντιλήμψεις and κυβερνήσεις are separate plural nouns in the list, not further specifications of "gifts of healing." Rendering them as "of helping, of guiding" makes them grammatically dependent on "gifts of," which misrepresents the Greek list structure. κυβερνήσεις also carries the sense of steering/administration, i.e., leadership.

text: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all work miracles?
Do all have gifts of healing? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret?
But eagerly desire the greater gifts. And yet I will show you a way that surpasses them all.

versions.text: But eagerly desire the greater gifts. And now I will show you a far better way.
versions.explanation: καὶ ἔτι is not temporal ("and now") but means "and yet, still more"; καθ' ὑπερβολήν is a strong superlative expression ("surpassing, beyond all measure"), stronger than "a far better way."
